facts.title: Placement and latency
facts.description: Workers placement describes where request handlers execute to reduce latency. Check the configured mode and each storage binding separately when documenting processing locations.

facts.title: Regional controls have a defined scope
facts.description: Regional Services for a configured custom domain can restrict TLS termination and Worker execution. The documentation excludes outgoing subrequests and some triggers, and says code and secrets remain globally deployed.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which Worker, storage bindings, logs and other Cloudflare products process data for this site?
What locations and transfer arrangements apply to this deployment, including outgoing requests and excluded triggers?
Which contracting entity, processing role, retention settings and customer agreement apply?

facts.title: Processing role depends on the activity
facts.description: Stripe describes both controller and processor activities. Review the product and processing purpose before describing its role for your site.

facts.title: Account and product context matter
facts.description: Stripe says the relevant entity can depend on account location, product and context. An SDK reference alone does not identify the entity or products used.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which payment, identity, fraud or connected-account products do you actually use, and which data reaches each?
For each activity, which Stripe entity and processing role apply under your account agreement?
Confirm actual processing locations, transfers and retention for the selected products. Do not infer these from an SDK import.

facts.title: Hosted and self-hosted deployments differ
facts.description: Supabase documents both hosted projects and deployments on your own infrastructure. A client library can connect to either, so a dependency match does not identify the hosting provider.

facts.title: The primary region is only part of the review
facts.description: Hosted projects have a primary region. Supabase distinguishes regional database data and backups from other processing, including account, support, usage and CDN activity that may occur elsewhere.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Is this hosted, self-hosted or a local development stack? Name the actual operators and products used.
Which primary project region and additional support, account, CDN or log processing locations apply?
Review backups, logs, deletion settings and the agreement for this deployment before recording retention and transfer facts.

facts.title: Sending region and storage are different
facts.description: Resend documents US storage for customer data, including message content, logs and webhook payloads. Choosing a sending region does not select a different storage region.

facts.title: Tracking is a separate setting
facts.description: Domain settings include optional open and click tracking. Confirm the settings actually used for each email flow before describing recipients and purposes.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which transactional or marketing flows use Resend, and what recipient data and message content do they contain?
Are open tracking, click tracking or webhooks enabled? Review each purpose and any applicable permission separately.
Confirm storage, transfers, plan-specific retention and deletion of logs, payloads and backups. Review the current DPA separately; its text was not retrieved for this reference.

facts.title: Authentication uses browser cookies
facts.description: Clerk documents cookies used by its authentication flow. Inventory the cookies and domains in your actual deployment, including custom session claims; this reference does not decide a legal exemption.

facts.title: Metadata can reach different readers
facts.description: Public metadata is frontend-readable; private metadata is backend-only; unsafe metadata can be written from the frontend. Review which fields your application stores and includes in session tokens.

facts.title: Customer records have separate terms
facts.description: Clerk distinguishes customer-submitted data from information covered by its own privacy policy. Review your customer agreement and data processing addendum for authentication records.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which sign-in fields, identity providers, metadata and session claims does this application use?
Which cookies and domains are actually used, and what are their lifetimes and assessed purposes?
Which entity, agreement, locations, retention and deletion process apply to your customer records?

facts.title: Function regions and delivery differ
facts.description: Vercel documents configurable Function regions and separate global static delivery. Review overrides, failover and middleware as well as databases and external services before describing processing locations.

facts.title: Log exports have their own destinations
facts.description: Vercel provides build, runtime, activity and audit logs. Runtime retention depends on the plan and observability settings; log drains can export data to other services.

facts.title: Check the plan and customer agreement
facts.description: The referenced Vercel addendum describes processing for customers on Enterprise and Pro plans. Confirm the agreement that applies to your account rather than assuming a public link establishes coverage.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which functions, middleware, storage and delivery services process visitor data, and in which configured regions?
What enters logs, how long is it kept, and which drain recipients or integrations receive copies?
Which plan, customer agreement and transfer arrangements apply to this deployment?

facts.title: Check automatic and explicit collection
facts.description: PostHog documents separate controls for autocapture, identified events and capture opt-in or opt-out. Confirm the enabled products, SDK settings and consent integration before describing the data collected.

facts.title: Replay needs its own review
facts.description: Replay has input masking, content controls and optional network capture. Test the actual pages and payloads, including headers and bodies; masking form fields does not describe every recording setting.

facts.title: Filtering after receipt is a different boundary
facts.description: PostHog distinguishes collection controls from transformations and IP-discard settings on its servers. Data that must never reach the provider needs to be excluded before transmission.

facts.title: A public DPA page is not your signed copy
facts.description: PostHog identifies its public DPA as a preview and directs customers to generate and countersign the agreement in their organization. Retain the agreement actually used.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which products, event properties, user identifiers, autocapture and replay settings are enabled?
How do actual loading, capture and withdrawal behave before and after a visitor changes their choice?
Where do events go, what is removed before transmission, and which retention and deletion settings apply?
Which customer agreement and transfer arrangements have you actually accepted and retained?

facts.title: Review the installed SDK and integrations
facts.description: Sentry documents collection that varies by runtime and integrations, including URLs, request data, identifiers and source maps. Check the installed SDK version, explicit user data and collection options; a monitoring label does not describe its payloads.

facts.title: Replay controls are separate
facts.description: Sentry documents replay masking, blocking, console and network capture controls separately from general SDK data-collection options. Test configured pages and enabled network details before enabling recording.

facts.title: Submitted events use the customer agreement
facts.description: Sentry distinguishes submitted Service Data from the information covered by its own privacy policy. Review the customer agreement and DPA for events sent from this application.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Which SDKs and integrations send events, request data, user identifiers, logs or source files?
Is replay enabled, and what do tests show for masking, console messages and network detail capture?
Which endpoint operator, account agreement, locations, retention and deletion settings apply?
